description: Door-v: is the residual between the GGM eq-49 q-difference module and its C1-tensor-square {+1,-1} realization a CONSTANT UNIPOTENT STOKES AUTOMORPHISM (monodromy datum)? Tests whether GGM_fundamental = (constant unipotent Stokes) x (TS-{+1,-1} fundamental) up to diagonal slope-scaling, via (1) convergence of the column-normalized transition That_m to a constant unipotent and (2) the basis-free R_m = T_m T_{m-1}^{-1} diagonal test, with a same-operator positive control validating the constancy detector.
computation: mpmath dps=70; C1 [m+2]_q b_{m+2}=b_{m+1}+b_m; growing carrier lift f+=[m]_q! b (~q^{+m^2/4}), decaying f-=b (~q^{-m^2/4}); TS-{+1,-1} frame (f+^2 slope+1, f-^2 slope-1); GGM y_{m+1}=(2-q^m)y_m-y_{m-1}, growing y_a forward + recessive via Miller backward from m=220; 2x2 value+shift Casoratian frames, columns normalized to unit max-abs (strips diagonal slope-scaling AND well-conditions the inverse whose raw cond ~ q^{m^2}); That_m on m=14..40, convergence on tail m=30..40; positive control = same-GGM-operator frame change (y_a,yrec) vs (y_b,yrec)

parameters.kill_criterion: That_m converges to a constant unipotent (tail entrywise drift < 1e-8, no diagonal sign oscillation) AND R_m=T_m T_{m-1}^{-1} off/diag < 1e-8 at substrate q, with the positive control passing the same bars => LANDS (constant unipotent Stokes datum); else scope-(a) REFUTED with residual structure reported

results.verdict: SCOPE-(a) REFUTED for the NONTRIVIAL-unipotent-Stokes hypothesis, WITH a sharp positive characterization of the residual.  Detector VALIDATED at substrate: the positive control (same GGM operator, two fundamental matrices differ by a genuine CONSTANT matrix) has R_m = T_m T_{m-1}^{-1} off/diag decaying geometrically ~q^{-m} to 0 (decay ratio 0.223485<0.5), confirming the R-diagonal test fires on a real constant-Stokes case; the substrate control shows NO (-1)^m diagonal character (its two frames are both GGM solutions). The comparison T_m = (col-normalized GGM frame)(col-normalized TS-{+1,-1} frame)^{-1} shows, at the substrate: (i) R_m = T_m T_{m-1}^{-1} off/diag decays geometrically ~q^{-m} to 0 (decay ratio 0.222872), IDENTICALLY to the genuine-constant control -- so the connecting matrix IS constant on the associated graded; (ii) the UNIPOTENT (off-diagonal Stokes) part is TRIVIAL, U[0,1],U[1,0] -> 0 (shrinking as ~q^{-m}: -0.0021136304, -0.0023579861) -- there is NO nontrivial Stokes jump; (iii) the SOLE residual is a DIAGONAL 2-torsion (-1)^m root-of-unity character (diag_sign_osc TRUE for the test, FALSE for the same-operator control) -- the sign GGM's growing solution carries (y_{m+1} ~ -q^m y_m) that the all-positive squares f+^2, f-^2 of the C1 tensor square structurally cannot.  So GGM and the TS-{+1,-1} projection have matching slopes AND matching theta/geometric magnitudes (off-diagonal ->0, diagonal ->unit) but differ by a Z/2 CHARACTER in the regular/torsion part of the irregular type -- a FORMAL-CLASS (gr) difference, NOT a Stokes (unipotent) datum, so RSZ Thm 5.5.7 does not bridge them.  Relation to the corpus integer-3: the -3 Stokes constant is GGM's OWN formal->actual jump (S^0=[[1,0],[-3,1]]); it does NOT appear in the TS->GGM comparison (whose unipotent part is trivial) -- the TS->GGM residual is a distinct 2-torsion character, so this construction does NOT reproduce the integer-3.  scope-(a) only; Door-i owns the module-level isoclinicity (b)-exclusion.
